meta.title: Sentence Analysis - Intermediate (B1-B2)
meta.description: A 30-question error identification test designed for intermediate English learners, featuring extended sentences and contexts relatable to Indonesian participants.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction. Choose No Error if correct.
questions.sentence: The group of students from Bandung are planning to visit the national museum on Monday morning.

multiErrorSegments.text: The group of students from Bandung

questions.explanation: Topic: Subject-Verb Agreement. The subject is 'The group' (a singular collective noun), so it requires the singular verb 'is', not 'are'. The prepositional phrase 'of students' does not change the subject's number.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: My mother bought many furnitures and a few equipments for our new house in Surabaya.

multiErrorSegments.text: for our new house in Surabaya.

questions.explanation: Topic: Countable and Uncountable Nouns. 'Furniture' and 'equipment' are uncountable nouns in English. They do not take an 's' and must be modified by quantifiers like 'much', 'a lot of', or 'some', not 'many' or 'a few'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: If the traffic jam in Jakarta will not clear up soon, we will be late for our important meeting.

multiErrorSegments.text: If the traffic jam in Jakarta

questions.explanation: Topic: First Conditional. In first conditional sentences, the 'if' clause uses the present simple tense ('does not clear up'), while the main clause uses the future simple ('will be'). 'Will' should not be used in the 'if' clause.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: He is looking forward to visit his grandparents in Yogyakarta and eating traditional gudeg with them.
questions.explanation: Topic: Gerunds and Infinitives. The phrase 'look forward to' requires a gerund (-ing form) because 'to' functions as a preposition here, not as part of an infinitive. Therefore, 'to visiting' is correct.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The traditional batik cloth was designed by a local artist and sell in many markets across Java.
questions.explanation: Topic: Passive Voice and Parallelism. The sentence describes two passive actions. To maintain parallel structure with 'was designed', the second verb must also be in the past participle form ('sold') or passive form ('is sold').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Rendang is considered as one of the most delicious food in the world, but some people finds it too spicy.

multiErrorSegments.text: Rendang is considered as one of the

questions.explanation: Topic: Superlatives and Subject-Verb Agreement. First, 'one of the' must be followed by a plural noun ('foods'). Second, 'people' is a plural noun, so it requires the plural verb 'find', not 'finds'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The teacher which gave us the assignment yesterday is very strict about the deadline.
questions.explanation: Topic: Relative Clauses. When referring to a person ('The teacher'), the relative pronoun 'who' must be used. 'Which' is reserved for animals and things.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: You should to bring your umbrella because it might raining later this afternoon.
questions.explanation: Topic: Modal Verbs. Modal verbs like 'should' and 'might' are always followed by the base form of the verb without 'to'. Therefore, 'should bring' and 'might rain' are correct.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Despite of the heavy rain, the football match was not cancelled by the referee.
questions.explanation: Topic: Conjunctions of Contrast. 'Despite' is a preposition and should not be followed by 'of'. The correct forms are either 'Despite the heavy rain' or 'In spite of the heavy rain'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: I have known my best friend since we are in elementary school together.
questions.explanation: Topic: Present Perfect and Past Simple. The main clause uses present perfect ('have known') to show an action continuing from the past. However, the 'since' clause refers to a specific completed period in the past, requiring the simple past tense ('were').

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The tour guide spoke very clear so that all the tourists can understand the history of Borobudur.
questions.explanation: Topic: Adjectives and Adverbs. The verb 'spoke' must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. 'Clearly' is the correct adverb form to describe how the guide spoke.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: He is studying hard to become an university professor in Surabaya.

multiErrorSegments.text: He is studying hard to become

questions.explanation: Topic: Articles. The word 'university' begins with a consonant sound (/j/), so it requires the indefinite article 'a', not 'an'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: We need to call off the meeting because the manager has come down with a flu.
questions.explanation: Topic: Phrasal Verbs and Articles. The idiomatic expression for becoming sick is 'come down with the flu' or 'come down with flu'. The definite article 'the' or no article is used, not 'a'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: My Indonesian friends usually are eating nasi goreng for breakfast on weekends.
questions.explanation: Topic: Adverb Placement. In the present continuous tense, adverbs of frequency like 'usually' are placed between the auxiliary verb ('are') and the main verb ('eating').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: There are not much chairs available in the classroom for the new students.
questions.explanation: Topic: Quantifiers. 'Chairs' is a plural countable noun, so it must be modified by 'many', not 'much'. 'Much' is used only with uncountable nouns.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The manager told me yesterday that he will review my application the next day.
questions.explanation: Topic: Reported Speech. When the reporting verb ('told') is in the past tense, the verb in the reported clause must be backshifted. 'Will' changes to 'would'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The traditional market is always very crowded in the weekend, especially on the morning.
questions.explanation: Topic: Prepositions of Time. We use 'on' (or 'at' in British English) for 'the weekend', and 'in' for parts of the day like 'the morning'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Between you and I, the new policy implemented by the school is quite unfair.

multiErrorSegments.text: by the school is quite unfair.

questions.explanation: Topic: Pronoun Case. Prepositions like 'between' must be followed by object pronouns. Therefore, 'me' is correct, not the subject pronoun 'I'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: Swim in the ocean near Bali can be dangerous during the rainy season.
questions.explanation: Topic: Gerunds. When a verb functions as the subject of a sentence, it must be in the gerund (-ing) form. 'Swimming' is the correct subject here.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: I do not know nothing about the traditional dance performance scheduled for tonight.
questions.explanation: Topic: Double Negatives. Standard English does not allow double negatives. Since 'do not' is already negative, 'nothing' must be changed to 'anything'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: I had my brother to fix my motorcycle because it was broken down.
questions.explanation: Topic: Causative Verbs. The active causative structure 'have + person + verb' requires the base form of the verb without 'to'. Thus, 'had my brother fix' is correct.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The police has arrested the thief who stole several luggages from the tourists.
questions.explanation: Topic: Collective Nouns and Uncountable Nouns. 'Police' is a plural collective noun requiring 'have'. 'Luggage' is uncountable and cannot be pluralized with 's'; use 'pieces of luggage' instead.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: I wish I have enough money to travel to Japan next summer.
questions.explanation: Topic: Wish Clauses. To express a wish about a present or future situation that is unlikely or untrue, we use the past simple tense ('had') after 'wish'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: She enjoys reading novels, watching movies, and to play traditional music.
questions.explanation: Topic: Parallel Structure. Items in a list must share the same grammatical form. Since 'reading' and 'watching' are gerunds, 'to play' must be changed to the gerund 'playing'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: If I was the president of Indonesia, I will improve the public transportation system.
questions.explanation: Topic: Second Conditional. For hypothetical or unreal present situations, the 'if' clause uses the past subjunctive ('were' for all subjects), and the main clause uses 'would' + base verb.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The local residents are very afraid from the upcoming volcanic eruption.
questions.explanation: Topic: Adjective + Preposition Collocations. The adjective 'afraid' is always followed by the preposition 'of', not 'from'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The coffee is too hot for me to can drink it right now.

correctAnswers: so hot that I cannot drink

questions.explanation: Topic: Too/Enough Structures. The structure 'too + adjective + for + object + to-infinitive' does not use modal verbs like 'can' inside the infinitive phrase. It should be 'for me to drink'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: Neither the manager nor the employees is happy with the new work schedule.
questions.explanation: Topic: Subject-Verb Agreement with Correlative Conjunctions. With 'neither/nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Since 'employees' is plural, the verb must be 'are'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The boring students were falling asleep during the very bored lecture.
questions.explanation: Topic: Participial Adjectives. '-ed' adjectives describe feelings (bored students), while '-ing' adjectives describe the cause of the feeling (boring lecture).

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Although the flight to Bali was delayed, we managed to arrive at the hotel before midnight.
questions.explanation: Topic: Conjunctions and Tense Consistency. No error. The sentence correctly uses 'although' to show contrast and maintains consistent past tense throughout.
